findings.evidence: PDF p.124 (book p.100): "the canonical 6–21-host fleet on the cloud rental basis is roughly $87.6K–$306.6K/month — the 6-host paid-occupancy $87,600 and the 21-host always-on $306,600 — (... the self-host 21-host line is a separate $155,816.93/month and lies outside this range ...)". The sidebar table (PDF p.99, book p.75) itself states the self-host line is "owned, not rented, so ~half the cloud 21-host line". 155,816.93 lies strictly inside the interval [87,600; 306,600], and its per-1K equivalent $24.97 (PDF p.99) lies inside the quoted $14.04–$49.13 per-1K range too.
findings.issue: The relational claim "lies outside this range" is arithmetically false under every reading: the self-host monthly total $155,816.93 is contained within the quoted cloud-rental range $87.6K–$306.6K, and its per-1K figure $24.97 is contained within $14.04–$49.13. The intended meaning ("is a separate cost basis, not a point in the cloud-rental series") is contradicted by the numbers as written, and it reverses the reader's check against the sidebar's "about half" comparison.
findings.fix_instruction: Replace "lies outside this range" with wording that names the category, not the interval, e.g. "is a separate capex+energy cost basis, not a point in this cloud-rental series" or "does not belong to the cloud-rental comparison above". Verify no other occurrence uses 'outside the range' for a value that numerically falls inside it.
